trust_decision.summary: Whether a password-verified login also needs a fresh, not-yet-used TOTP code. That would be decided in core user Authenticate. At the pinned commit it checks only the password, because TOTP does not exist yet, and the supplied fix.diff adds TOTP itself (totp.Validate with no replay tracking) rather than the reuse prevention.

landing_point.why: Authenticate is where login credentials are verified; after the feature commit it is where totp.Validate is called on login (fix.diff:3099).

out_of_scope_notes: fix.diff also carries unrelated changes (ptr.Of -> new(), golangci, go.mod bumps, nginx cfgfiles, docker/truenas/tailscale edits) that are not part of this advisory.
unverified: Mis-pinned host: the pinned tree has no TOTP code at all (no 'totp' match in any .go file) and fix.diff introduces the TOTP feature (fix.diff:3093-3104, fix.diff:3996-4011). The diff contains no reuse prevention, so the vulnerability does not exist at the pinned commit and the supplied diff is not the published fix.

The actual reuse-prevention fix exists in latest: latest/internal/business/domain/user/service.go:70-78 (login) and :382 (activate) call latest/internal/database/domain/user/repository.go:252-260 TryUpdateLastUsedTOTPCode, an atomic conditional UPDATE, plus migrations latest/internal/database/core/migrations/scripts/{sqlite,postgres}/031_totp_reuse_prevention.up.sql. It is probably commit 8d35e1e, but the commit identity was not checked.

Re-screening is recommended with the pin set to the parent of the actual reuse-prevention commit. That host would have two entry points (login, TOTP activate), a repository/converter layer (save/reload of last-used codes via the Save path) and a TOCTOU race. It might fit Pattern A, but none of this was checked against a correct pin.
